args.message:
Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212

The implementation used ROUND_HALF_UP despite the docstring and
tests/test_money.py expecting half-even rounding. This caused the
nightly build to fail on values such as Decimal("2.665"), which should
round to 2.66 rather than 2.67.

files.content:
# Changelog

## Unreleased

- Fix `round_money` to use banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`) as required by FIN-212.

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
## Problem

The nightly build was failing on `tests/test_money.py`. `round_money` in `src/money.py` was implemented with `ROUND_HALF_UP`, even though its docstring — and FIN-212 — require banker's rounding (`ROUND_HALF_EVEN`).

This caused values with an exact half-cent to round away from zero instead of to the nearest even digit:

- `round_money(Decimal("2.675"))` → expected `2.68` (both modes agree)
- `round_money(Decimal("2.665"))` → expected `2.66`, got `2.67`

## Change

- `src/money.py`: import and use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` instead of `ROUND_HALF_UP`.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: note the fix under Unreleased.

## Verification

CI on `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding` (run `ci-0001`, sha `ed19cae5f5`): **passed**.

## Notes

One behavior change is visible to callers: half-cent amounts can now round down as well as up, which is the intended FIN-212 behavior. Merge requires code-owner approval per repo policy.
